footnotes: From pre-tax income to net income: after $1.2M of other items after tax.

Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC (income statement lines as the filing presents them); free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue fell 6.3% to $2.2B in 2025. Gross margin was 36.8%, versus 34.6% a year earlier, and operating income fell 0.3% to $42.8M, a 1.9% margin.
Net income was $732K, or $0.03 per share, after a $118M loss a year earlier. Operating cash flow was $180M and free cash flow $91.8M, versus $125M; ICU Medical returned $8.8M through buybacks.
sources: ICU Medical, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)

risks: We derive a significant portion of our revenues from non-U.S. sales and from products manufactured at our non-U.S. facilities…
If we are unable to compete successfully with our competitors, we may be unable to maintain market share, in which case our sales may not grow…
If demand for our products were to decline significantly, we might not be able to recover the cost of our expensive automated molding…
Product development requires substantial investment that may be difficult for us to fund…
Significant changes in U.S. trade, tax or other policies that restrict imports or increase import tariffs for certain countries…
Continuing pressures to reduce healthcare costs and inadequate coverage and reimbursement may adversely affect our prices and volume
